seg_p0042_s0001: Similarly, in Dorotheus's Synopsis as well, we read that Aristobulus was made bishop of Britain; and in the fragment which is published under the name of Heleca, bishop of Saragossa: "Among the Britons the memory of many martyrs is celebrated, especially of St. Aristobulus, one of the seventy-two disciples, who was also called Zebedee (father of James, and of John the martyr, of Mary Salome), who went to Rome with Peter. Then, leaving his household behind, sent into England as bishop, he died a martyr in the second year of the most savage emperor Nero." For so it stands on page 108 of the Saragossa edition. But what I enclosed in the parenthesis must be corrected thus: "Father of James and John, husband of Mary Salome." For on the following page Concordia, the wife of the apostle Peter, is reported to have been the daughter of Aristobulus and Salome. "St. Peter," says the author, "is held in honour in Spain, and his wife Concordia suffered at Rome under Nero, not long before he himself suffered. She was, as M. Maximus teaches in his commentaries on the epistle of St. Peter, the daughter of Aristobulus, or Zebedee, and of Salome; and the mother-in-law also of Andrew, who married another sister of Concordia and of James and John. Now Aristobulus, surnamed Zebedee, was the brother of Barnabas, the apostle of the Lord." Thus he writes; and with him, concerning Peter's taking to wife the daughter of Aristobulus, the brother of the apostle Barnabas, the Greeks too agree — in Metaphrastes, in his commentary on Peter and Paul, and in the Menaia, under the day of June 29.
seg_p0042_s0002: At the end of the latter epistle to Timothy, Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia are mentioned together by the apostle.
seg_p0042_s0003: Pseudo-Clement intimates that Linus, the first bishop of the Roman Church, ordained by Paul, was the son of Claudia.
seg_p0042_s0004: The Book of the Pontiffs, however, asserts that the father of Linus was a certain Herculanus. Our own writers gather from the poet Martial that Claudia was British by nationality and the wife of Pudens; for he sang of Claudia thus: Although Claudia Rufina is sprung from the woad-blue Britons, why does she possess the heart of the Latin people?
